design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial where participants were randomized to bupropion SR or identical placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation concealment was preserved with numbered bottles concealed from patients and staff, and baseline characteristics between groups were well-balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Numbered study bottles were supplied by the study coordinator and remained concealed from the patients and medical staff.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was double-blind using identical placebo tablets, compliance was similar between groups, and analysis was conducted on an intention-to-treat basis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The participants were instructed to take the study pill, bupropion SR, 150 mg, or identical placebo, once a day for 3 days, and then twice a day for 2 months... Primary efficacy and safety analyses were performed on an intent-to-treat basis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up was nearly complete with only 1 patient lost to follow-up per arm (2 of 151 total, >98% retention).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 151 patients were enrolled; all but 2 completed follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although smoking abstinence was self-reported without biochemical verification, participants and outcome assessors were double-blinded to intervention status, making differential measurement bias unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary efficacy outcome measure was self-reported continuous abstinence from smoking 1 year after the index hospitalization... reported quitting status was not confirmed by an objective method, such as a carbon monoxide concentration in exhaled air, we could not exclude false reporting of abstinence

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was stopped early following an interim analysis of 150 participants instead of the planned 250 without predefined early stopping rules reported, and no prospectively published statistical analysis plan or protocol registration was cited.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Approximately 250 participants were needed in order to have a 2-sided α level of .05 and a power of 0.80 to detect such a difference. Interim analysis was performed after recruitment of 150 patients.

overall_summary: The study had low risk of bias across randomization, deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, and outcome measurement due to good blinding and high retention; however, some concerns exist regarding selection of the reported result because recruitment was terminated early after an interim analysis without explicit pre-specified stopping boundaries or pre-registration.

design_rationale: The study is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial where participants were randomly assigned to bupropion SR or placebo using computer-generated randomly-permuted blocks.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, stratified and blocked, and centrally concealed by the study pharmacist from enrollment staff, with baseline characteristics well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Using a computer program, the study statistician generated a sequence of randomly-permuted blocks of 4 within strata formed by study site and daily cigarette consumption (<10 vs >10). The study pharmacist used this sequence, concealed from enrollment staff, to assign participants to study arm.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of participants and key study personnel was maintained with an identical placebo, co-interventions were balanced, and primary analyses followed an intention-to-treat approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Subjects were randomly assigned to sustained-release bupropion or identical placebo... Subjects and study personnel, except the statistician and pharmacist, were blind to treatment assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although 33% did not complete the 1-year follow-up, loss to follow-up was identical across groups (23% lost + ~10% withdrew in both arms) and handled using standard intention-to-treat smoking-cessation imputation (missing participants classified as smoking), which is robust to differential bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 165 (67%) of 248 enrolled patients completed one-year follow-up (Figure 1)... Subjects were considered smokers if they were lost to follow-up, failed to provide a saliva sample, or had a cotinine concentration >20 ng/ml.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was objectively confirmed by biochemical validation (saliva cotinine concentration) and assessed in a double-blind trial where outcome assessors were masked to intervention allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measure was 7-day point-prevalence tobacco abstinence 1 year after discharge. Self-reported abstinence was validated by saliva cotinine. Subjects were considered smokers if they were lost to follow-up, failed to provide a saliva sample, or had a cotinine concentration >20 ng/ml.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, and results are reported fully according to pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes and pre-specified analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov (#NCT0018181)... The primary outcome measure was 7-day point-prevalence tobacco abstinence 1 year after discharge.

overall_summary: The trial demonstrated sound methodological quality across all domains, featuring central computerized random allocation with concealment, robust double-blinding, standard ITT handling of missing data in smoking cessation research, and biochemically validated outcomes.

design_rationale: The study is a multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial where participants were randomly assigned (1:1) via a centralized internet website using random permuted blocks stratified by center.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization was centralized via a website using random blocks and stratified by center, ensuring sequence generation and concealment, with baseline characteristics well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was done via an internet website using random blocks of 2 and 4 and was stratified by center to ensure that similar numbers of patients were randomized to the 2 arms of the study at each study center.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind with identical placebo pills prepared by an independent pharmacist, interventions were delivered as planned alongside standard counseling, and analysis adhered to the intention-to-treat principle.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Bupropion and identical placebo tablets were purchased from Sandoz Canada Inc. (Boucherville, Quebec, Canada). An independent industrial pharmacist was responsible for coating, bottling, and packaging the medication for distribution to collaborating sites.

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing data rates were balanced between groups (~22% lost/withdrew) and handled according to the standard, conservative intention-to-treat assumption in smoking cessation trials (missing = smoking), supported by per-protocol sensitivity analyses showing consistent results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because loss to follow-up rates >30% are not unusual in smoking cessation trials (8,18), our ITT analysis assumed that those who withdrew consent or were lost to follow-up had returned to smoking at their baseline rates.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessment was objective and biochemically validated via exhaled carbon monoxide in a double-blind trial, preventing measurement bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Smoking status assessment consisted of a self-report of smoking in the previous 7 days and biochemical validation by measurement of exhaled carbon monoxide (CO) levels. A threshold of exhaled CO ≤10 ppm on a CO monitor (Micro 4 Smokerlyzer, Bedfont Scientific Ltd., Rochester, United Kingdom) was used to confirm smoking abstinence (17).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT00689611), and the reported primary and secondary outcomes and analyses correspond directly to the prespecified protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The ZESCA (Zyban as an Effective Smoking Cessation Aid for Patients Following an Acute Coronary Syndrome) trial (NCT00689611) was a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial... The primary end point was point prevalence smoking cessation at 12 months.

overall_summary: This was a well-designed and conducted double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial with central web-based randomization, biochemically validated smoking abstinence, and pre-registered analyses with standard handling of missing data, resulting in a low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to bupropion or placebo using a computer algorithm to generate a random list of treatment assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated random sequence was used, but the method of allocation concealment prior to assignment is not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We assigned participants to the two study arms by using a computer algorithm to generate a random list of treatment assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was double-blind using an identical-appearing placebo with blinded personnel, identical co-interventions (counseling), and intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants randomized to the control arm of the study received an identical-appearing placebo. All study personnel engaged in providing interventions to participants were blinded to treatment assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up rates were high (83/85 included in ITT analyses, with 2 deaths), and standard conservative imputation assuming missing participants were smoking was applied.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The two participants lost to follow-up and the seven participants who dropped out of the study were considered smokers in analyses that required biochemical or spousal confirmation of quitting.

domain_judgments.rationale: Smoking abstinence was objectively verified using salivary cotinine assays (with sensitivity analyses for spousal proxies), and outcome assessors were blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For participants who reported that they had quit smoking at the end of treatment and at the 6-month telephone interview, we obtained saliva samples for cotinine testing.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-published analysis plan is cited, though standard predefined smoking cessation outcomes are reported across all follow-up timepoints.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We determined on-medication, end-of-medication, 3-month, and 6-month smoking cessation rates.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to lack of details regarding allocation concealment in the randomization process and the absence of an explicit prospective trial registration protocol.
